data.name: Chapter 5: Equipment
entries: The cities of {@i Star Wars} are diverse and multicultural, varying dramatically by planet and system. Commonplace activities in one city might be taboo in another. The most common species on one planet might be shunned on the next one. Every city, in addition to the climate and cultures, varies dramatically in the options available for sale.

In addition to those options available in the {@i Player's Handbook}, adventurers might encounter new and interesting wares. On some planets, and in some cultures, armor is made from unique materials that grant it interesting properties. On other planets, a more diverse armory might be available for purchase—or theft. In other places still, interesting and unique adventuring implements might be discovered.

entries.name: Starting Equipment
entries: When choosing the starting equipment for your class, you might have an option to choose any of a certain type of item. For instance, berserkers get a choice of "{@i (a)} a martial {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon} and a light or medium physical {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} or {@i (b)} two martial {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}". When choosing starting equipment in this fashion, the items available in this chapter should not be included. However, if you use instead use the Variant: Starting Wealth by Class rule, the items in this chapter should be considered available for purchase.

entries.name: Ammunition
entries: {@filter Blasters|items|firearm=true} that deal energy or ion damage use {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, while {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true} that deal kinetic damage use slug cartridges. This chapter introduces {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true} that deal new damage types: acid, fire, and sonic. These weapons also use {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}.

entries.name: Buying and Selling Treasure
entries: This chapter introduces armor, weapons, adventuring gear, and other valuable materials. Like those options found in the {@i Player's Handbook}, selling these items should generally be possible, provided they are unspoiled.

entries.name: Enhanced Items
entries: Enhanced items are scarce and powerful, leading to them rarely having a predetermined price. Buying and selling enhanced items can rarely be performed easily, often requiring extensive time and credits to find a potential buyer and seller.

entries.name: Rare Materials
entries: While rare materials, as the name indicates, are more scarce than their raw material counterparts, they typically have a commonly accepted value across markets. While they won't always be available for sale, they will usually fetch the same price across worlds.

entries.name: Armor and Shields
entries: Adventuring through the different worlds of {@i Star Wars} shows limitless variety across cultures, varying drastically by their values and technological availability. Many cultures create similar items, but using different materials, granting their items a unique flair. The Armor table shows some examples of how commonly available types of armor found in the game differ, depending on the materials used.
The Armor table shows the cost, weight, and other properties of these types of armor worn in the worlds of {@i Star Wars}.

entries.name: Armor and Shield Proficiency
entries: Anyone can put on a suit of armor or wield a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}. Only those proficient in the armor's use know how to wear it effectively, however. Your class gives you proficiency with certain types of armor. If you wear armor that you lack proficiency with, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on any {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} that involves Strength or Dexterity, and you can't force- or tech-cast.
If you have proficiency in armor, you have proficiency in the appropriate {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} as well.

entries.name: Armor Class (AC)
entries: Armor protects its wearer from attacks. The armor (and {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}) you wear determines your {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Armor Materials
entries: In addition to form and function, armor varies greatly based on material. Beyond those standard materials universally available to armor, you might find armor made with more specialized and scarce materials. Armor made with these materials offers a unique strength, but also a weakness. Additionally, the armor's cost increases by an amount, based on the armor's type, as shown in the Armor Type Cost Increase table below:
Only physical {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shields} can be crafted using alternative armor materials. Additionally, barding can be created using alternative armor materials.

entries.name: Multiple Materials
entries: Armor and shields can be made using an amalgam of materials. Doing so increases the cost of the armor or {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} for each material used in its creation, and the number of materials used can't exceed half the crafter's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, rounded up.

entries.name: Beskar
entries: Armor and shields made from beskar gains the regulated property, but also the strength 11 property. If the armor or {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} would already have the strength property, instead increase the strength number by 2.

entries.name: Bone
entries: Bone armor and shields have the barbed (1d4) and spiked (1d4) properties, respectively, but suffer a -1 penalty to {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Crystadium
entries: Armor and shields made from crystadium has the absorptive 1 property, but also the rigid and imbalanced properties, respectively.

entries.name: Durafiber
entries: Durafiber armor and shields have their strength number reduced by one step (from 19 to 17, 17 to 15, 15 to 13, or 13 to 11). If the strength number is 11, this removes the strength property from it entirely. If the armor or {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} lacks the strength property, it instead gains the lightweight property. Additionally, durafiber armor and shields suffer a -1 penalty to {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Duranium
entries: Armor and shields made from duranium gain the reactive 1 and responsive 1 properties, respectively, but also the cumbersome property.

entries.name: Durasteel
entries: Durasteel armor has the impermeable 2 and rigid properties. Durasteel {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shields} have the interlocking and imbalanced properties.

entries.name: Duravlex
entries: Armor and shields made from duravlex have the silent and concealing properties, respectively, but suffer a -1 penalty to {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Fleximetal
entries: Fleximetal armor and shields gain the avoidant 1 property, but also the strength 11 property. If the armor or {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} would already have the strength property, instead increase the strength number by 2.

entries.name: Laminanium
entries: Armor and shields made from laminanium gain the obscured and lambent properties, respectively, but also the cumbersome property.

entries.name: Neutronium
entries: Neutronium armor and shields gain the insulated 1 property, but also the strength 11 property. If the armor or {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} would already have the strength property, instead increase the strength number by 2.

entries.name: Plastoid
entries: Armor made from plastoid has the reinforced and rigid properties. Shields made from plastoid have the anchor and imbalanced properties.

entries.name: Quadanium
entries: Quadanium armor and shields gain the charging 1 property, but also the cumbersome property.

entries.name: Armor Properties
entries: Many armors and shields have special properties related to their use, as shown in the Armor table. You must be proficient in and wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} to benefit from its special properties.

entries.name: Absorptive
entries: When you are wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, damage that you take from weapons is reduced by an amount equal to the absorptive number. If this would reduce the damage to 0, the damage is instead reduced to 1.

entries.name: Agile
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, your Dexterity score becomes equal to the agile number. If your Dexterity is already equal to or greater than the agile number, it has no effect on you.

entries.name: Anchor
entries: A {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property can be used to {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|provide cover}. As an action, you can anchor or recover the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}. While anchored, you gain no benefit from a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, and it does not require the use of a hand. Instead, while anchored, a light {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} provides one-quarter {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, a medium {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} provides {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|half cover}, and a heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} provides three-quarters {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}.

entries.name: Avoidant
entries: When wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property and a creature makes an attack against you, the {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range decreases by an amount equal to the avoidant number, to a minimum of 1.

entries.name: Barbed
entries: When you succeed on a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check to initiate or maintain a grapple while wearing armor with this property, the creature takes kinetic damage using the barbed damage (which appears in parentheses with the property) + your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Charging
entries: When you take damage while wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you gain a charge. You can store a maximum number of charges equal to the charging number, and the charges last for 1 minute. The next time you hit with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} while you have charges, you deal additional damage of the same type as the weapon's damage equal to the number of charges stored, and the charges are expended.

entries.name: Concealing
entries: While wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Cumbersome
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced by 5.

entries.name: Gauntleted
entries: While wearing armor with this property, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} deal kinetic damage using the gauntleted damage (which appears in parentheses with the property) + your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Imbalanced
entries: When you are critically hit while wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you can't take reactions until the start of your next turn, and you gain no AC benefit from your {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} against the next attack against you before the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Impermeable 2
entries: Armor with this property includes the limited functions of a number of enviromental suits equal the impermeable number from the list below, which are either included in parentheses with the property or determined by the GM. Additionally, it includes 4 hours' capacity of oxygen, which can be replenished by oxygen tanks.

items: {@b Chemical Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Corroded|sw5e-phb|corroded} condition.
{@b Conductive Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} condition.

{@b Dampening Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} condition, and you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sound.
{@b Diving Suit:} You are protected from the hazards associated with high pressure environments.
{@b Flame-Proof Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Ignited|sw5e-phb|ignited} condition.
{@b Hazard Suit:} You are immune to the {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb|poisoned} condition.

{@b Mind-Shielding Suit:} You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid having your mind read or affected.
{@b Space Suit:} You are protected from the hazards associated with low pressure environments.

{@b Stabilizer Suit:} You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being moved.

entries.name: Insulated
entries: When you make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against an effect that would deal ion or lightning damage while wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of below the insulated number as the insulated number.

entries.name: Interlocking
entries: While wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property within 5 feet of a friendly creature who is also wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you can both use your reactions on either of your turns to interlock the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shields}. While interlocked, both creatures gain a bonus to AC equal to the interlocking number. If at any point the creatures are more than 5 feet from each other, the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shields} immediately de-interlock, and this effect ends.

entries.name: Lambent
entries: While wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to activate or deactivate the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}'s light. While active, the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet. Additionally, Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks made while the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}'s light is active that rely on sight have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Lightweight
entries: Armor and shields with this property have their weight reduced by half.

entries.name: Magnetic
entries: While you are wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property and a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} misses you by an amount less than or equal to your bonus to AC from your {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, the attacking creature must make a Strength check, DC equal to the magnetic number. On a failed save, the creature's weapon adheres to the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}. As an action, a creature can repeat this check. On a success, the weapon is freed.

entries.name: Obscured
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, electronic sensors and cameras have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) checks against you that rely on sight.

entries.name: Powered
entries: While wearing armor with this property, your Strength score becomes equal to the powered number. If your Strength is already equal to or greater than the powered number, it has no effect on you.

entries.name: Reactive
entries: When you are wearing armor with this property and a creature hits you with an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you gain a bonus to AC against the next attack from that creature before the start of your next turn equal to the reactive number.

entries.name: Regulated
entries: When you are wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property and a creature rolls the maximum on a weapon damage die against you, they must reroll and use the new roll, even if the new roll is the maximum on the weapon damage die.

entries.name: Reinforced
entries: When you make a long jump while wearing armor with this property, you can {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} a number of feet up to twice your Strength score. When you make a high jump, you can leap a number of feet up into the air equal to 3 + twice your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Responsive
entries: While you are wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property and an attack misses you by an amount less than or equal to your bonus to AC from your {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, you gain a bonus to AC against the next attack from that creature before the start of your next turn equal to the responsive number.

entries.name: Rigid
entries: While wearing armor with this property, you add half your Dexterity modifier (rounded down), instead of your full Dexterity modifier, to Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} you make. If your Dexterity modifier is negative, you instead subtract the full modifier.

entries.name: Silent
entries: While wearing armor with this property, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sound.

entries.name: Spiked
entries: When you succeed on a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check to shove or trip a creature while wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, the creature takes kinetic damage using the spiked damage (which appears in parentheses with the property) + your Strength modifier. If you use a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property as an improvised weapon, the damage increases by one step (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, or {@dice d8} to 2d4).

entries.name: Steadfast
entries: While wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength checks and Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being moved.

entries.name: Versatile
entries: A {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} with this property can be used with one or two hands. While wielded in two hands, you gain an additional bonus to AC equal to the versatile number.

entries.name: Weapons
entries: In addition to armor varying across myriad planets, you might find new and unique types of weaponry available. Your weapon proficiencies reflect the tools you are most likely to use. The Weapons tables show additional weapons used in the worlds of {@i Star Wars}, their price and weight, the damage they deal when they hit, and any special properties they possess.

entries.name: Weapon Proficiency
entries: Your species, class, and feats can grant you proficiency with certain weapons or categories of weapons. The three types of weapons—{@filter blaster|items|firearm=true}, {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}, and {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon}, are further broken down into two categories—simple and martial. Proficiency with a weapon allows you to add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} for any attack you make with that weapon. If you make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} using a weapon with which you lack proficiency, you do not add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.
Proficiency in these weapons is discussed further in {@book chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6}.

entries.name: Weapon Properties
entries: Many weapons have special properties related to their use, as shown in the Weapons table.

entries.name: Biting
entries: This weapon's damage becomes acid. Additionally, when you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} with a weapon with the biting property, you can instead force the target to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon, or the biting number, whichever is lower). If you would have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and if you would have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes normal weapon damage and is subjected to any additional effects that would occur on a hit, and the first attack it makes before the end of its next turn has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. If damage dealt by this weapon reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it must make a DC 13 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it dies immediately without making {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}. A disintegrated creature and everything unenhanced it is wearing and carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A creature destroyed in this way can not be revitalized.

entries.name: Bright
entries: This weapon's damage becomes fire, and its luminous property sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet while activated, instead of only dim light in a 5-foot radius. Additionally, when you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} with a weapon with the bright property, you can instead force the target to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon, or the bright number, whichever is lower). If you would have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and if you would have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes normal weapon damage and is subjected to any additional effects that would occur on a hit, and the creature takes additional damage of the same type at the start of its next turn equal to your governing ability modifier.

entries.name: Brutal
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a weapon with the brutal property, you roll a number of additional weapon damage dice equal to the brutal number.

entries.name: Corruption
entries: This weapon's damage becomes necrotic, and it loses the luminous property if it has it. Additionally, when you would make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} with a weapon with the corruption property, you can instead force the target to make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon, or the corruption number, whichever is lower). If you would have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and if you would have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, the creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the target takes normal weapon damage and is subjected to any additional effects that would occur on a hit, and the creature cannot regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Defensive
entries: When you make your first attack on your turn with a weapon with the defensive property, you can choose to suffer a penalty to attack and damage rolls with that weapon up to the defensive number. If you do so, you gain the same bonus to AC. These effects last until the start of your next turn, as long as you're holding the weapon.

entries.name: Dire
entries: Before you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the dire property, you can choose to suffer a penalty to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} up to the dire number. If you do so and you hit with it, you gain an equivalent bonus to the damage roll.

entries.name: Disarming
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a weapon with the disarming property against a creature that is holding an object, you can attempt to disarm the target (no action required). If the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), it must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or it drops an object of your choice at its feet.

entries.name: Disintegrate
entries: When a creature is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} by a weapon with the disintegrate property, it must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, DC equal to the disintegrate number. On a failed save, it dies immediately without making {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}. A disintegrated creature and everything unenhanced it is wearing or carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A creature destroyed in this way can not be revitalized.

entries.name: Disruptive
entries: When a creature is forced to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} due to taking damage from a weapon with the disruptive property, the DC for the check equals 10 or the full damage taken, whichever number is higher, instead of only half.

entries.name: Keen
entries: When you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the keen property, the {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range increases by an amount equal to the keen number.

entries.name: Mighty
entries: When making an attack with a mighty weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

entries.name: Neuralizing
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon with the neuralizing property, you can force it to make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, DC equal to the neuralizing number. On a failed save, the creature takes an additional 1d4 psychic damage and becomes {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Piercing
entries: Before you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the piercing property, you can choose to gain a bonus to the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} up to the piercing number. If you do so and you hit with it, you suffer an equivalent penalty to the damage roll.

entries.name: Reckless
entries: When you make your first attack on your turn with a weapon with the reckless property, you can choose to gain a penalty to AC up to the reckless number. If you do so, you gain the same bonus to attack and damage rolls with that weapon. These effects last until the start of your next turn, as long as you're holding the weapon.

entries.name: Shocking
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon with the shocking property, you can force it to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, DC equal to the shocking number. On a failed save, the creature takes an additional 1d4 lightning damage and becomes {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Silent
entries: When you make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} with a weapon with the silent property while hidden, it does not automatically reveal your presence. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) check contested by your targets' Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) check. On a success, you remain hidden.

entries.name: Smart
entries: This weapon ignores your Dexterity score and {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. Two numbers appear in parentheses with the property—the first is the weapon's Dexterity score, and the second is the weapon's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. The weapon uses these values instead of yours when you make attack and damage rolls with it. If you lack proficiency with the weapon, the weapon does not benefit from its {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Sonorous
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon with the sonorous property, you can force it to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, DC equal to the sonorous number. On a failed save, the creature takes an additional 1d4 sonic damage and becomes {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Switch
entries: A weapon with the switch property can deal an alternate type of damage. A damage value appears in parentheses appears with the property-the damage when the weapon uses its alternate damage type. On your turn, you can use your object interaction to change the weapon's damage type.

entries.name: Vicious
entries: Whenever you deal damage with a weapon with the vicious property and roll the maximum on a weapon damage die, you gain a bonus to damage equal to the vicious number.

entries.name: Special Weapons
entries: Weapons with special rules are described below.

entries.name: Flechette Cannon
entries: The flechette cannon does not make {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}. Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the flechette cannon uses specialized projector tanks, which, when fired, spray an area with the contents of the tank. Projector tanks require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the tank—s effects. It can have different ammunition types loaded simultaneously, and you can choose which ammunition you—re using as you fire it (no action required). If you don—t meet the flechette cannon—s strength requirement, creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If you lack proficiency in the flechette cannon, you must roll the damage dice twice and take the lesser total.

entries.name: Grenade Launcher
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the grenade launcher fires grenades. When firing a grenade at long range, or if you don—t meet the grenade launcher—s strength requirement, creatures within the radius of the grenade—s explosion have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If you lack proficiency in the grenade launcher, you must roll the damage dice twice and take the lesser total.

entries.name: Rocket Launcher
entries: Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the rocket launcher fires specialized projectiles in the form of rockets. When firing a rocket at long range, or if you don—t meet the rocket launcher—s strength requirement, creatures within the radius of the rocket—s explosion have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Shoulder Blaster
entries: Mounted by the shoulder slot, a shoulder {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} does not require a free hand to use. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being disarmed of this weapon.

entries.name: Shoulder Cannon
entries: Mounted by the shoulder slot, a shoulder cannon does not require a free hand to use. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} and {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to avoid being disarmed of this weapon.

entries.name: Vapor Projector
entries: The vapor projector does not make {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}. Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, the vapor projector uses specialized projector tanks, which, when fired, spray an area with the contents of the tank.

Projector tanks require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the tank—s effects. It can have different ammunition types loaded simultaneously, and you can choose which ammunition you—re using as you fire it (no action required). If you don—t meet the vapor projector—s strength requirement, creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. If you lack proficiency in the vapor projector, you must roll the damage dice twice and take the lesser total.

entries.name: Focuses
entries: For both force- and tech-casting, there exist focuses which are used to channel their respective powers. While focus generators are optional for forcecasters, techcasters are required to have a focus in order to cast their powers. Wristpads are traditionally worn on the wrist and do not require a hand to activate, while focus generators generally take the form of a small scepter or crystal that is traditionally held in the hand.

entries.name: Focus Proficiency
entries: Unlike weapons and armor, no proficiency is required to use focuses. Instead, you need the ability to forcecast for focus generators and the ability to techcast for wristpads.

entries.name: Variant: Alternative Focuses
entries: While traditionally there are only two types of focuses—focus generators and wristpads—certain class features and enhanced items unlock the ability to use an alternative item type. If a character wants to use something else as their focus, such as a lightsaber or a heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, consider allowing them to do so. Later in this chapter, you'll find rules to add casting properties to unenhanced focuses. As GM, you can consider extending these rules to weapons and armor, or even tools for your engineer, as you deem appropriate. Additionally, there are a significant number of focus generator and {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} modifications that grant these properties. If a player wants to use an alternative focus, consider allowing them to use focus generator and {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} modifications to in place of the normal modifications for the item they're using as a focus. If they do so, the DC to install or remove a modification, as shown in the Installation/Removal DC by Rarity table in this chapter is increased by 5. You should also consider allowing engineers to install these mods in their archetype focus, even if there is no existing chassis for that item.

entries.name: Casting Properties
entries: Some focuses have special properties related to their use, as shown in the Data Recording and Storage subsection of the Adventuring Gear section.

entries.name: Absorbing
entries: While using this item as your focus, when you take damage from any source, you can reduce that damage by an amount up to the absorptive number, provided you have a number of force or tech points equal to half the damage absorbed. When you do so, you lose half the damage taken in force or tech points.

entries.name: Accessing
entries: While using this item as your focus, you gain access to a number of new powers (chosen by the GM) of a combined total no greater than the access number. The powers count as known by you, and you can't unlearn the powers.

entries.name: Amplifying
entries: While using this item as your focus, your {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range with melee force or tech attacks increases by an amount equal to the amplifying number.

entries.name: Bolstering
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Focus generator property} While using this item as your focus, your maximum force points increase by the bolstering number.

entries.name: Constitution
entries: While using an item with this property as your focus, you gain no benefit from any additional properties the item has unless your Constitution score meets or exceeds the constitution number.

entries.name: Dispelling
entries: While using this item as your focus, your level of proficiency in force- or tech-casting {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} increases by a number of steps equal to the dispelling number (to trained, from trained to proficient, from proficient to {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise}, from {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} to mastery, from mastery to high mastery, or from high mastery to grand mastery).

entries.name: Elongating
entries: While using this item as your focus, when you cast a power that affects a cylinder, the height of the cylinder increases by an amount equal to the elongating number, and the radius of the cylinder increases by an amount equal to half the elongating number.

entries.name: Enlarging
entries: While using this item as your focus, when you cast a power that affects a cube, the length of each side of the cube increases by an amount equal to the enlarging number.

entries.name: Expanding
entries: While using this item as your focus, when you cast a power that affects a cone, the length of that cone increases by an amount equal to the expanding number.

entries.name: Extending
entries: While using this item as your focus, when you cast a power that affects a line, the length of the line increases by an amount equal to the extending number, and the width of the line increases by an amount equal to half the extending number.

entries.name: Fading
entries: While using this item as your focus, the critical fail range of force or {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that require a Strength or Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} increases by an amount equal to the fading number.

entries.name: Focused
entries: While using this item as your focus, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}.

entries.name: Increasing
entries: While using this item as your focus, when you cast a power that has a range of 5 feet or greater, the range of that power increases by an amount equal to the increasing number.

entries.name: Adding Casting Properties to Focuses
entries: Each of these properties can be used to create a new unenhanced focus generator {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. When generating new focuses for player character use, each positive property should be offset by a level of Constitution, and each property should increase the of the focus by 1,000 cr. This cost scales by the number of properties and it is in addition to the base cost of the time. For instance, a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} with one positive property and the Constitution 11 property would cost 1,600 cr (1,000 cr for the positive property + 600 for the base cost of the {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}). A {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} with two positive properties and the Constitution 13 property, however, would cost 3,600 cr (1,000 cr for the first property, 2,000 cr for the second property, and 600 for the base cost of the {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}). GMs can generate new focuses in this way, similar to how the Weapon Calculator can be used to generate new weapons at the discretion of the GM. Unenhanced focuses can't exceed 1 level in a single property.

entries.name: Inflating
entries: While using this item as your focus, when you cast a power that affects a sphere, the radius of the sphere increases by an amount equal to the inflating number.

entries.name: Mitigating
entries: While using this item as your focus, using the {@action Ready|sw5e-phb} action to cast a force or {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} no longer requires {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration}. You can only have one instance of this feature active at a time. Additionally, if the power would not be released, and the power was 1st level or higher, the cost of the power is reduced by a number of points equal to the mitigating number, to a minimum of 1.

entries.name: Ranging
entries: While using this item as your focus, your {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range with ranged force or tech attacks increases by an amount equal to the ranging number.

entries.name: Rending
entries: While using this item as your focus, the critical fail range of force or {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that require a Dexterity or Intelligence {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} increases by an amount equal to the rending number.

entries.name: Repelling
entries: While using this item as your focus, your powers are no longer automatically dispelled or interrupted. Instead, the DC to interrupt or dispel your powers is equal to 10 + the power's level, or 8 + half your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your casting modifier for that power, whichever is greater.

entries.name: Storing
entries: While using this item as your focus, you can store 1st-level or higher powers of a combined total no greater than the storing number within the focus for later use. You can cast a power into this item while touching it. The power has no effect other than to be stored in the item. If the item can't hold the power, the power is expended without effect. You can cast any power stored in it at its base level, causing the power to no longer be stored, freeing up the space.

entries.name: Surging
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb} property} While using this item as your focus, your maximum tech points increase by the surging number.

entries.name: Withering
entries: While using this item as your focus, the critical fail range of force or {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} that require a Wisdom or Charisma {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} increases by an amount equal to the withering number.

entries.name: Variant: Focus Properties and Features
entries: Many of these properties could affect class features. Consider extending those properties to benefit those features, as appropriate.

entries.name: Corrosive Cartridge
entries: A corrosive cartridge is a specialized {@item Slug cartridge|sw5e-phb|slug cartridge} for use with {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapons that deal kinetic damage. When you hit with a shot with the loaded weapon, the creature must make a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, taking 1d8 acid damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. If you reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} with the loaded weapon, it must make a DC 13 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it dies immediately without making {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}. A disintegrated creature and everything unenhanced it is wearing or carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A creature destroyed in this way can not be revitalized.

entries.name: Cryo Cell

The loaded weapon deals cold damage instead of its normal damage type, and when you hit with a shot the creature must make a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature takes 1d4 cold damage and gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage and isn't {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed}. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, that creature is frozen in carbonite for 1 hour.

As an action, you can prime and throw a grenade at a point you can see within 30 feet + your Strength modifier x 5. The grenade explodes, setting the ground in a 10-foot radius ablaze for 1 minute. The fire ignites any flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.

When a creature enters the fire or starts its turn there, it creature must make a DC 14 Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. The creature takes 2d8 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Grenade, Panic

Each creature within 10 feet must make a DC 14 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 2d6 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much as on a successful one.

Additionally, on a failed save, a creature becomes {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you for 1 minute. At the start of an affected creature's turn, it can repeat this save, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Grenade, Stun
entries: Grenades can be set to detonate on impact or with a timer that causes them to explode on {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} count 20 (losing all {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} ties). As an action, you can prime and throw a grenade at a point you can see within 30 feet + your Strength modifier x 5. Each creature within 10 feet must make a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature is {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the end of their next turn.

Additionally, on a failed save, a creature is {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb|unconscious} for 1 minute, until it takes damage, or until someone uses an action to shake or slap the creature awake. At the end of an affected creature's turn, it can repeat this save, ending the effect on a success.

Mines can be set to detonate when a creature comes within up to 15 feet of it or paired with a {@item Remote detonator|sw5e-phb|remote detonator}. As an action, you can prime and set a mine on a surface you can reach, which arms at the start of your next turn. When detonated, each creature within 15 feet of it must make a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. A creature takes 2d8 acid damage on a failed save, or half as much as on a successful one. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it must make a DC 13 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, it dies immediately without making {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|death saving throws}. A disintegrated creature and everything unenhanced it is wearing or carrying are reduced to a pile of fine gray dust. A creature destroyed in this way can not be revitalized.

entries.name: Underwater Respirator
entries: Underwater respirators are worn over the mouth and lower face. While worn, you can breath underwater, as the {@item Respirator|sw5e-phb|respirator} filters the water to create breathable oxygen. The {@item Respirator|sw5e-phb|respirator} functions for 1 hour per {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} (to a maximum of 2 hours) and can be recharged by a power source or replacing the {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}.

entries.name: Water Suit
entries: Water suits are sealed suits that prevent water from getting in or out. Additionally, while wearing a water suit, you can breath underwater, as the suit filters the water to create breathable oxygen.

entries.name: Prosthetics
entries: These cybernetic augmentations don't count against the maximum cybernetic augmentations you can support, but they do count towards your total cybernetics augmentations as shown in the Cybernetic Augmentations Side Effects table. Rules for installing augmentations can be found in chapter 7.
{@b {@i Arm Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces a single arm, forearm, and hand.
{@b {@i Ear Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces an ear.
{@b {@i Eye Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces an eye.
{@b {@i Facial Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces all or part of a damaged face.
{@b {@i Foot Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces a foot.
{@b {@i Forearm Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces a forearm and hand.
{@b {@i Hand Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces a hand.
{@b {@i Leg Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces a leg and a foot.
{@b {@i Throat Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces a throat, including a creature's voice, though it does not grant a creature the ability to speak beyond their species' capabilities.
{@b {@i Torso Prosthesis.}} This cybernetic augmentation replaces all or part of a damage torso.

entries.name: Camtono
entries: A camtono is a secured, handle container used for transporting valuable goods. A camtono comes with one key. Without the key, unlocking the camtono requires a DC 15 {@item Security kit|sw5e-phb|security kit} to force open. It stores 5 lb., not exceeding 1/4 cubic foot, has an AC of 10, and 15 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. Destroying the camtono risks damaging any goods stored inside.

entries.name: Smugglepack
entries: This {@item Backpack|sw5e-phb|backpack} comes with a main compartment that stores 15.00 lb., not exceeding 1/2 cubic foot. Additionally, it has a hidden storage compartment that stores 5 lb., not exceeding 1/4 cubic foot. Finding the hidden compartment requires a DC 15 {@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb} check.

entries.name: Computer Spike
entries: When you make an Intelligence ({@item Slicer's kit|sw5e-phb|slicer's kit}) check, you can use the spike (no action required) to reroll the check. You must use the new roll. You can wait until after you roll the {@dice d20} before deciding to use the spike, but you must decide before the GM says whether the check succeeds or fails.

This belt has slots to hold 60 slug cartridges, and can be connected to directly fuel a single {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapon that uses slug cartridges. Once per turn, if the powered weapon would be reloaded, it can be done without using an action using any ammunition in the belt. Connecting or disconnecting a weapon takes an action. Replacing 10 slug cartridges takes an action.
entries.name: Ammo-feed Belt
Holster
entries: A holster can be worn on the leg, hip, or back, and can be used to store a single weapon. You can draw a weapon stored in a holster without using an action. Once you've done so, you can't do so again until you store a weapon in the holster as an action.

entries.name: Power Belt
entries: This belt has slots to hold six {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, and can be connected to directly power a single {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapon that uses {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}. Once per turn, if the powered weapon would be reloaded, it can be done without using an action using any ammunition in the belt. Connecting or disconnecting a weapon takes an action. Replacing an expended {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} takes an action.

entries.name: Rocketpack
entries: Rocketpacks combine the aerial transportation of a {@item Jetpack|sw5e-phb|jetpack} with the firepower of a rocket launcher. Activating or deactivating the rocketpack's flight capabilities requires a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} and, while active, you have a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} of 25 feet. The {@item Jetpack|sw5e-phb|jetpack} last for 1 minute per {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb} (to a maximum of 5 minutes) and can be recharged by a power source or replacing the {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}.

Additionally, your rocketpack comes with an integrated rocket launcher with the Ammunition (range 100/400) and reload 1 properties. Rather than traditional {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, this rocket launcher fires specialized projectiles in the form of rockets. Whenever you would make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you can instead fire this rocket launcher. When firing a rocket at long range, creatures within the radius of the rocket's explosion have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. Reloading this rocket launcher takes 1 minute.

entries.name: Tools
entries: A tool helps you to do something you couldn't otherwise do, such as craft or repair an item, pick a lock, or slice into a computer. Your species, class, background, or feats give you proficiency with certain tools. Tool use is not tied to a single ability, since proficiency with a tool represents broader knowledge of its use. Like skills, proficiency with a tool allows you to add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to checks you make with it. Unlike skills, you must have your tools present in order to make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with them.

The table shows examples of some of the most common types of tools. Each tool falls under one of four categories: artisan's implements, gaming sets, musical instruments, or specialist's kits. Each tool requires a separate proficiency.

entries.name: Artisan's Implements
entries: Artisan's implements are predominantly designed for building and crafting things of permanent nature. Each set of implements focuses on a specific craft.
{@b {@i Artist's Implements.}} Artist's implements encompasses any set of tools designed to create art.
{@b {@i Audiotech's Implements.}} Audiotech's implements are for crafting and tuning musical instruments.
{@b {@i Constructor's Implements.}} Constructor's implements are for creating and fortifying structures.
{@b {@i Cybertech's Implements.}} {@item Cybertech's implements|sw5e-phb} are used for crafting and modifying wristpads.
{@b {@i Geneticist's Implements.}} Geneticist's implements are for creating and grafting genetic mutations.
{@b {@i Jeweler's Implements.}} Jeweler's implements are used to appraise gemstones and create jewelry.
{@b {@i Surveyor's Implements.}} Surveyor's implements are used to create both physical and digital maps.
{@b {@i Synthweaver's Implements.}} Synthweaver's implements create and modify articles of clothing.
{@b {@i Writer's Implements.}} Writer's implements contains everything needed to create and publish physical and digital written works.

entries.name: Gaming Sets
entries: This item encompasses a wide range of game pieces, including dice and/or decks of cards. A few common examples appear on the Tools table, but other kinds of gaming sets exist.

entries.name: Musical Instruments
entries: Several of the most common types of musical instruments are shown on the table as examples. Musical instruments can often be used in place of—or in addition to—a performance.

entries.name: Specialist's Kits
entries: Like artisan's implements, specialist's kits are need to pursue a craft or trade. Some specialist's kits are used to craft items that are impermanent, such as grenades, medpacs, or poisons while other tools are used to achieve a specific purpose, such as picking locks or creating a disguise.
{@b {@i Alchemist's Kit.}} Alchemist's kits contains everything needed to enhance creatures and items with alchemy.
{@b {@i Archaeologist Kit.}} Archelogist kits contains instruments used to collect gems and relics.
{@b {@i Artillerist's Kit.}} Artillerist's kits contains all the necessary tools to create, repair, and modify turrets.
{@b {@i Bioanalysis Kit.}} Bioanalysis kits contains a variety of instruments to harvest and store plants and herbs.
{@b {@i Brewer's Kit.}} Brewer's kits contains a variety of devices and containers to adequately distill and house liquors and beers.

{@b {@i Munitions Kit.}} Munitions kits contains the necessary tools to create ammunition for {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true}, as well as devices to hone {@filter lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} and {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}.
{@b {@i Scavenging Kit.}} Scavenging kits contains the necessary implements to harvest and scavenge ores and metals.
{@b {@i Spicer's Kit.}} Spicer's kits contains the required tools to create and refine illicit substances.

entries.name: Trade Goods
entries: Trade is an essential part of the galactic economy. Many spacers make their living buying and selling goods along hyperspace routes that connect the galaxy's major worlds.

A merchant may be chartered by an individual or a corporation to deliver goods to a certain port, or move goods along a specified route. During times of war, opportunities abound in the shipping of ammunition and medical supplies. Some traders, seeking to earn a quick profit, may resort to smuggling illegal or restricted cargo on behalf of one of the galaxy's many crime syndicates. The Trade Goods table shows the value of commonly exchanged goods.

entries.name: Substances
entries: Substances, most commonly coming in the alcohol and spice varieties, are goods often sought after by the more seedy denizens of the {@i Star Wars} underworld. Whether legal or not, people search for these wares, whether to consume or profit on.

entries.name: Consumption
entries: Consuming substances offers powerful temporary boons in the form of a high, potentially offset by a subsequent low. Additionally, consuming substances regularly risks addiction, which reduces the efficacy of substances until a creature abstains from using them.

entries.name: Highs and Lows
entries: Each substance offers a high followed immediately by a potential low. For the duration of the high, a creature might gain a bonus to an ability score, temporary force or tech points, or some other boon. Immediately when the high ends, the character must succeed on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} depending on the substance or suffer a longer-lasting low, which reverses the effects. The high and low varies depending on the substance consumed, and the duration of the high and low vary based on the rarity of the substance consumed, as determined in the item's description.

A creature can only benefit from one substance at a time. If a creature consumes an additional unit of a substance, while currently experiencing a high or a low, they must immediately make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the effects of addiction before applying the benefits of the consumed substance. Consuming a substance while experiencing a low immediately ends the low, but any time remaining in that low is added to the duration of the low of the additional consumed substance.

Consuming substances regularly also risks becoming addicted to a substance. When the low of a substance ends, a creature must make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, determined by what substance they are coming off of, as determined in the substance's description. Addiction is measured in six levels. An effect can give a creature one or more levels of addiction, as specified in the effect's description.

entries.caption: Addiction Level
rows: The duration of lows is doubled.
The duration of highs is halved.
The duration of lows is quadrupled, instead of doubled.
The effect of highs is halved.
The effect of lows is maximized.
The effect of highs is minimized.

entries: If an already addicted creature suffers another effect that causes addiction, its current level of addiction increases by the amount specified in the effect's description.

A creature suffers the effect of its current level of addiction as well as all lower levels. For example, a creature suffering level 2 addiction has the duration of its lows doubled, and the duration of its highs halved.
An effect that removes addiction reduces its level as specified in the effect's description, with all addiction effects ending if a creature's addiction level is reduced below 1.

If a creature abstains from consuming a substance for 24 hours, they can make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to reduce their addiction level by 1, provided they've completed a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} during that 24 hours. The DC for the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} equals 10 + the creature's addiction level. On a success, their addiction level is reduced by 1. For instance, a creature suffering addiction level 3 can abstain from consuming any substance for 24 hours. If they do so, and they complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} during that 24 hour period, they can make a DC 13 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a success, their addiction level is reduced to 2.

entries.name: Availability
entries: While alcoholic beverages are legal on most planets, spices are not. Whether or these items are readily available is up to your GM.

entries.name: Alcoholic Beverages
entries: The alcoholic beverages are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Deuterium-pyro
entries: This alcoholic beverage, favored amongst ruffians, features a terrible flavor and strong aftertaste. As an action, you can apply this substance to a creature within 5 feet. For the next minute, the creature experiences a high that allows them to roll an additional d3 when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Strength. At the end of the high, the creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or experience a low that lasts 10 minutes, during which they must roll a d3 and subtract the result when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Strength. At the end of the low, the creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist addiction.

entries.name: Mummergy
entries: Mummergy is a strong-smelling liquor derived from a plant of the same name. As an action, you can apply this substance to a creature within 5 feet. For the next minute, the creature experiences a high that allows them to roll an additional d3 when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Intelligence. At the end of the high, the creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or experience a low that lasts 10 minutes, during which they must roll a d3 and subtract the result when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Intelligence. At the end of the low, the creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist addiction.

entries.name: Novanian Grog
entries: This grog features a pungent odor and a strong kick. As an action, you can apply this substance to a creature within 5 feet. For the next minute, the creature experiences a high that increases their current and maximum tech points by 2d3. At the end of the high, the creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or experience a low that lasts 10 minutes, their current and maximum tech points are reduced by 2d3. At the end of the low, the creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist addiction.

entries.name: Raava
entries: Raava is a traditional liquor breed from zsajhira berries. As an action, you can apply this substance to a creature within 5 feet. For the next minute, the creature experiences a high that allows them to roll an additional d3 when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Dexterity. At the end of the high, the creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or experience a low that lasts 10 minutes, during which they must roll a d3 and subtract the result when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Dexterity. At the end of the low, the creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist addiction.

entries.name: Spicebrew
entries: Spicebrew, a popular drink across the galaxy, is a tanned alcoholic beverage topped with foam. As an action, you can apply this substance to a creature within 5 feet. For the next minute, the creature experiences a high that increases their current and maximum force points by 2d3. At the end of the high, the creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or experience a low that lasts 10 minutes, their current and maximum force points are reduced by 2d3. At the end of the low, the creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist addiction.

entries.name: Tihaar
entries: This colorless spirit, favored by Mandalorians, burns the mouth and throat when consumed. As an action, you can apply this substance to a creature within 5 feet. For the next minute, the creature experiences a high that allows them to roll an additional d3 when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Constitution, and at the start of each of the creature's turns it gains 2d3 temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. At the end of the high, the creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or experience a low that lasts 10 minutes, during which they must roll a d3 and subtract the result when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Constitution, and for the duration their current and maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} are reduced by 2d3. If this would reduce your maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} below 1, it instead becomes 1. At the end of the low, the creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist addiction.

entries.name: Tsiraki
entries: Tsiraki is a blue-colored alcoholic beverage crafted from fermented salakberries and pickling spices. As an action, you can apply this substance to a creature within 5 feet. For the next minute, the creature experiences a high that allows them to roll an additional d3 when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Charisma. At the end of the high, the creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or experience a low that lasts 10 minutes, during which they must roll a d3 and subtract the result when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Charisma. At the end of the low, the creature must make a DC 14 Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist addiction.

entries.name: Vayerbok
entries: Vayerbok is a thick, green, vegetable-based alcoholic beverage typically served hot. As an action, you can apply this substance to a creature within 5 feet. For the next minute, the creature experiences a high that allows them to roll an additional d3 when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Wisdom. At the end of the high, the creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or experience a low that lasts 10 minutes, during which they must roll a d3 and subtract the result when making an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} using Wisdom.
