data.name: Chapter 6: Customization Options
entries: The combination of ability scores, species, class, and background defines your character's capabilities in the game, and the personal details you create set your character apart from every other character. Even within your class and species, you have options to fine-tune what your character can do. But this chapter is for players who—with the GM's permission—want to go a step further.

This chapter expands on feats, which are special options you can choose instead of increasing your ability scores as you gain levels. Your GM decides whether these options are available in a campaign.

entries.name: Fighting Styles and Masteries
entries: Wretched Hives introduces new ammunition types, such as the specialized {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells}, or rockets. You'll want to extend the benefits of certain Fighting Styles and Fighting Masteries to these new munitions, as explained below.

entries.name: Explosives Style and Mastery
entries: You will want to extend the benefits of this pair to include rockets.

entries.name: Area Style and Mastery
entries: You will want to extend the benefits of this pair to include flechette clips, flechette mags, and projector tanks.

entries.name: Gunning Style and Mastery
entries: You'll want to extend the benefits of this pair to include specialized {@item Power cell|sw5e-phb|power cells} and slug cartridges.

entries.name: Class Proficiencies
entries: Certain classes, such as fighters or guardians, gain proficiency in all weapons within a specific category. For instance, fighters gain proficiency in {@filter all blasters|items|firearm=true} and {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}, and guardians gain proficiency in {@filter all lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} and {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}. Monk, operative, scholar, and sentinel, on the other hand, only gain proficiency in {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} that meet certain criteria. If that criteria is met due to the use of an item or feature that add—or remove—a referenced property, this does not grant that class proficiency in the weapon. For instance, operatives gain proficiency in {@filter simple blasters|items|firearm=true|weaponcategory=simple}, {@filter simple vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon|weaponcategory=simple}, martial {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true} that lack the auto, special, strength, and two-handed properties, martial {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon} with {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property}. If they add {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property} to a {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon}, or remove the strength property from a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapon, this would not grant the operative proficiency in that weapon.

entries.name: Feats
entries: A feat represents a talent or an area of {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} that gives character special capabilities. It embodies training, experience, and abilities beyond what a class provides. At certain levels, your class gives you the Ability Score Improvement feature. Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking that feature to take a feat of your choice instead. You can take each feat only once, unless the feat's description says otherwise.

You must meet any prerequisite specified in a feat to take that feat. If you ever lose a feat's prerequisite, you can't use that feat until you regain the prerequisite. For example, the Inspiring Leader feat requires you to have a Charisma of 13 or higher. If your Charisma is reduced below 13 somehow—perhaps by a withering curse—you can't benefit from the Inspiring Leader feat until your Charisma is restored.

entries.name: Augmented Cyborg
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Type beast or humanoid} You've experimented with cybernetic augmentations, granting the following benefits:

items: Increase an ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Choose one cybernetic augmentation of standard rarity from Appendix A. That augmentation is installed and doesn't count against the maximum cybernetic augmentations you can support, but it does count towards your total cybernetics augmentations as shown in the Cybernetic Augmentations Side Effects table in Chapter 7.

entries.name: Customized Droid
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Type droid} You've been customized beyond other droids of the same model, granting the following benefits:

items: Increase an ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Choose one droid customization of standard rarity from Appendix A. That customization is installed and doesn't count against the maximum droid customizations you can support, but it does count towards your maximum parts or protocols, as appropriate.

entries.name: Investigative Attunement
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level} You've spent a significant amount of time appraising and testing enhanced items. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase an ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} made to identify items.

Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can choose one object that you must touch for 10 minutes. If it is an enhanced or modified item, you learn its properties and how to use them, whether it requires attunement to use, and how many charges it has, if any. You learn whether any powers are affecting the item and what they are. If the item was created by a power, you learn which power created it.

entries.name: Muscled Menace
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Strength 13, size Medium} Despite being of otherwise average size, your might extends beyond that of your peers. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You can't add more than +3 when determining your bonus to AC from your Dexterity.
You can't add more than +3 when determing your bonus to Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} from Dexterity.

You gain the Oversized special trait: {@b {@i Oversized.}} Light- and vibro-weapons that lack the dexterity or light property are considered to have the heavy property for you. The strength number for {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true} is reduced by one step (from 19 to 17, 17 to 15, 15 to 13, or 13 to 11). If the strength number is 11, you ignore it entirely.

entries.name: Savage Shorty
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Strength 13, size Small} Despite being short of stature, your size has no impact on your strength and virility. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You lose the Undersized special trait.

entries.name: Tiny Terror
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} Strength 13, size Tiny} Despite falling below knee height of other species, your size has less impact on your strength and virility. You gain the following benefits:

items: Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You lose the Pintsized special trait, and you are no longer limited to +3 when determining your bonus to attack and damage rolls for weapon attacks using Strength due to the Puny special trait.

You gain the Undersized special trait: {@b {@i Undersized.}} Your small stature makes it hard for you to wield bigger weapons. You can't use heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shields} or {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} with the two-handed property unless it has the light property, and if a martial weapon has the versatile property, you can only wield it in two-hands.

entries.name: Weapon Focused
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level} You adopt a particular type of weapon as your focus. Choose one of the weapon focus options, detailed later in this chapter. You can take this feat multiple times.

entries.name: Weapon Supremacist
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 4th level} You've mastered a particular type of weapon. Choose one of the weapon supremacist options, detailed later in this chapter. You can take this feat multiple times.

entries.name: Weapon Focus
entries: The Weapon Focused feat offers your choice of weapon focus. You can't take a weapon focus option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: Alternative Weapon Focus
entries: Your weapon of choice may be governed by one weapon focus, whereas your character can be better realized utilizing a different focus. For instance, your {@item Blaster rifle|sw5e-phb} might work better for you with Carbine Focus rather than Rifle Focus. Work with your GM to determine if a different focus is better suited, and mechanically appropriate, to your character's identity. A weapon's focus and supremacy must match.
You may choose your weapon focus from the following options or roll on the table below to determine it randomly.

entries.name: Weapon Classifications
entries: Each weapon has a classification, as shown in Weapons by Class table later in this chapter, that determines which weapon focus it is governed by.

entries.name: Blade Focus
entries: You've focused your combat training on blade weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's damage rolls.

When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the weapon, the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} the target makes before the start of your next turn has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.
When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b parry}. For each attack you forgo, you gain a +1 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Carbine Focus
entries: You've focused your combat training on carbine weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's damage rolls.

When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the weapon, the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} the target makes before the start of your next turn has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to  {@b startle}. For each attack you forgo, you expend 1 ammunition and choose a creature that is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property)  and is within your weapon's normal range. The creature must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or become {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Crushing Weapon Focus
entries: You've focused your combat training on crushing weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's damage rolls.
When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the weapon, you add the attack's governing ability modifier twice, instead of once, to the attack's damage.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b shatter} the ground. For each attack you forgo, choose a separate 5-foot square within your weapon's reach to shatter. That square becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} until cleared. Each 5-foot-square portion of the area requires at least 1 minute to clear by hand. Additionally, each creature other than you in an affected square must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon). On a failed save, a creature takes damage equal to the attack's governing ability modifier.

entries.name: Heavy Weapon Focus
entries: You've focused your combat training on heavy weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's damage rolls.
When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the weapon, you add the attack's governing ability modifier twice, instead of once, to the attack's damage.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b suppress}. For each attack you forgo, you expend ammunition equal to half your weapon's reload number (minimum of 2) and choose a 10-foot-cube area within your weapon's normal range. Each creature in the area that is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property) must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or become {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Polearm Focus
entries: You've focused your combat training on polearm weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's damage rolls.
When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the weapon, you can roll one additional weapon damage die.
When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one of your attacks to {@b choke up}. If you do so, your reach increases by 5 feet until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Rifle Focus
entries: You've focused your combat training on rifle weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's damage rolls.
When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the weapon, you can roll one additional weapon damage die.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to  {@b scramble}. For each attack you forgo, you can move up to 10 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

entries.name: Sidearm Focus
entries: You've focused your combat training on sidearm weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's damage rolls.

When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the weapon, the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} made against the target before the start of your next turn has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b daze} a creature. For each attack you forgo, you expend 2 ammunition and choose a creature that is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), has a head, and is within your weapon's normal range. The creature must succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or become {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} until the end of its next turn or until it takes damage, whichever happens first.

entries.name: Trip Weapon Focus
entries: You've focused your combat training on trip weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's damage rolls.

When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the weapon, the next {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} made against the target before the start of your next turn has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b interrupt}. For each attack you forgo, one creature within your reach gains no benefit to {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class} from its {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Weapon Supremacy
entries: The Weapon Supremacist feat offers your choice of weapon supremacy. You can't take a weapon supremacy option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

entries.name: Alternative Weapon Supremacy
entries: Your weapon of choice may be governed by one weapon supremacy, whereas your character can be better realized utilizing a different supremacy. For instance, your {@item Blaster rifle|sw5e-phb} might work better for you with Carbine Supremacy rather than Rifle Supremacy. Work with your GM to determine if a different supremacy is better suited, and mechanically appropriate, to your character's identity. A weapon's focus and supremacy must match.
You may choose your weapon supremacy from the following options or roll on the table below to determine it randomly.

entries.name: Weapon Classifications

entries.name: Blade Supremacy
entries: You've specialized your combat training with blade weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

Whenever you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and hit and the lower of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also hit (or a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and the higher of the two d20s would also fail), and the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), it must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or gain 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the start of your next turn.
Your {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} range increases by 1.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b parry}. For each attack you forgo, you gain a +1 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn. If you could already parry, instead you can do so as your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

Whenever you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and hit and the lower of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also hit (or a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and the higher of the two d20s would also fail), and the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), it must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or gain 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level until the start of your next turn.

You can wield this weapon in one hand. When you do so, you treat the weapon as if it would have the strength 11 property. If the weapon already has the strength property, its strength number increases by one step (from 11 to 13, 13 to 15, 15 to 17, 17 to 19, or 19 to 21). While wielding the weapon in one hand, you can't attack a target beyond the weapon's normal range.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to  {@b startle}. For each attack you forgo, you expend 1 ammunition and choose a creature that is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property)  and is within your weapon's normal range. The creature must succeed on a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or become {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked} until the start of your next turn. If you could already startle, instead you can do so as your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Crushing Weapon Supremacy
entries: You've specialized your combat training with crushing weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

Whenever you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and hit and the lower of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also hit (or a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and the higher of the two d20s would also fail), and the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), it must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or it is pushed 5 feet in a direction of your choice.

Once per round, when you use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b shatter} the ground. For each attack you forgo, choose a separate 5-foot square within your weapon's reach to shatter. That square becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} until cleared. Each 5-foot-square portion of the area requires at least 1 minute to clear by hand. Additionally, each creature other than you in an affected square must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon). On a failed save, a creature takes damage equal to the attack's governing ability modifier.  If you could already shatter, instead you can do so as your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries: You've specialized your combat training with heavy weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

Whenever you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and hit and the lower of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also hit (or a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and the higher of the two d20s would also fail), and the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), it must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or it is pushed 5 feet in a direction of your choice.

When a creature rolls a 1 on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against one of these weapons, they treat the effect's damage as if it had rolled the maximum. If a creature would already treat the effect's damage as if it had rolled the maximum when it rolls a 1 on this weapon's {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, it instead does so on a roll of 1 or 2.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b suppress}. For each attack you forgo, you expend ammunition equal to half your weapon's reload number (minimum of 2) and choose a 10-foot-cube area within your weapon's normal range. Each creature in the area that is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property) must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or become {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb|frightened} of you until the end of their next turn. If you could already suppress, instead you can do so as your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Polearm Supremacy
entries: You've specialized your combat training with polearm weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

Whenever you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and hit and the lower of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also hit (or a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and the higher of the two d20s would also fail), and the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the weapon's damage roll.

When you make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against an effect that would shove or trip you, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of below half your level (rounded up) as half your level.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one of your attacks to {@b choke up}. If you do so, your reach increases by 5 feet until the start of your next turn. If you could already choke up, instead you can do so as your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Rifle Supremacy
entries: You've specialized your combat training with rifle weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

Whenever you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and hit and the lower of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also hit (or a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and the higher of the two d20s would also fail), and the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the weapon's damage roll.

Your ranged weapon attacks reduce partial {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} by one step (from three-quarters to half or half to one-quarter) against targets within 30 feet of you. If the target has one-quarter {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, you ignore it entirely.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to  {@b scramble}. For each attack you forgo, you can move up to 10 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}. If you could already scramble, instead you can do so as your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Sidearm Supremacy
entries: You've specialized your combat training with sidearm weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

Whenever you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and hit and the lower of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also hit (or a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and the higher of the two d20s would also fail), and the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), it must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or it drops an object of your choice. If you have a free hand and the object is within your reach, you catch the object. Otherwise, it lands at your feet.

You can now reload these weapons using your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} or object interaction, instead of just your action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}. You must have one free hand to reload.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b daze} a creature. For each attack you forgo, you expend 2 ammunition and choose a creature that is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), has a head, and is within your weapon's normal range. The creature must succeed on a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or become {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb|incapacitated} until the end of its next turn or until it takes damage, whichever happens first.  If you could already daze, instead you can do so as your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries: You've specialized your combat training with trip weapons. You gain the following benefits while wielding any of these weapons, if you are proficient with it:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to the weapon's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls}.

Whenever you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} and hit and the lower of the two {@dice d20} rolls would also hit (or a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and the higher of the two d20s would also fail), and the target is no more than one size larger than you (your size or smaller if your weapon has the light property), it must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to attacks with the weapon) or it drops an object of your choice. If you have a free hand, you catch the weapon. Otherwise, it lands at your feet.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) checks and {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made to trip a creature.

When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action, you can choose to forgo one or more attacks to {@b interrupt}. For each attack you forgo, one creature within your reach gains no benefit to {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|armor class} from its {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} until the end of its next turn. If you could already interrupt, instead you can do so as your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

data.name: Chapter 7: Enhanced Items
entries: The ability to plunder enhanced items from the hoards of conquered pirates, or discover them in long-lost Sith tombs is an experience players expect. Such items grant capabilities a character could rarely have otherwise, or they complement their owner's capabilities in wondrous ways.

entries.name: Rarity
entries: Each enhanced item has a rarity: standard, premium, prototype, advanced, legendary, or artifact. Standard enhanced items are the most plentiful. Consequently, higher rarity items are more scarce. The game assumes that the secrets of creating the most powerful items arose centuries ago and were then gradually lost as a result of wars or mishaps. Even premium items can't be easily created. Thus, many enhanced items are unique and well-preserved relics.

Rarity provides a rough measure of an item's power relative to other enhanced items. Each rarity corresponds to a character level, as shown below in the Enhanced Item Rarity and Identification table. A character doesn't typically find a prototype enhanced item, for instance, until 5th-level or later. That said, rarity shouldn't get in the way of your campaign's story. If you want the darksaber to fall into the hands of 1st-level character, so be it. No doubt a great story will arise from that event.

If your campaign allows for trade in enhanced items, rarity can also help you set prices for them. As the GM, you determine the value of an individual enhanced item based on its rarity. Suggested values are provided in the Enhanced Item Rarity table. The value of a consumable, such as a {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac} or stimpac, is typically half the value of a permanent item of the same rarity.

entries.name: Identifying Enhanced Items
entries: Some enhanced items have properties not readily distinguishable to the naked eye. Identifying such an item requires use of the {@i analyze} or {@i telemetry} power, or inspection with the appropriate tools.

If a player is proficient in the appropriate type of tools, as shown in the Tools by Item Tools by Item table in this chapter, they can make a check with the tools to identify the properties of an enhanced item over the course of a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}. To use this benefit, they must have the tools, and the enhanced item must be within reach. The DC is found above in the Enhanced Item Rarity and Identification table.

entries.name: Variant: Simpler Identification
entries: If you prefer enhanced items to be more readily identifiable, you can allow characters to identify enhanced items through experimentation. Over the course of a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, a character can focus on one enhanced item while being in physical contact with it. At the end of the {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, the character learns the item's properties, as well as how to use them.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: Some enhanced items require a creature to form a bond with them before their enhanced properties can be used. This bond is called attunement, and certain items have a prerequisite for it. If the prerequisite is a class, a creature must be a member of that class to attune to the item.

Without becoming attuned to an item that requires attunement, a creature gains only its unenhanced benefits. For example, an enhanced heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} that requires attunement provides the benefits of a normal heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} to a creature not attuned to it, but none of its enhanced properties.

Attuning to an item requires a creature to spend an uninterrupted {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} focused on only that item while being in physical contact with it. This focus can take the form of weapon practice, meditation, or some other appropriate activity. At the end of the {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, the creature gains an intuitive understanding of how to activate any enhanced properties of the item, including any necessary command words.

An item can be attuned to only one creature at a time, and a creature can be attuned to a maximum number of items equal to their {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}; any attempt to attune to an additional item fails. Standard, premium, and prototype items cost one attunement slot, while advanced, legendary and artifact cost two.

A creature's attunement to an item ends if the creature no longer satisfies the prerequisites for attunement, if the item has been more than 100 feet away for at least 24 hours, if the creature dies, or if another creature attunes to the item. A creature can also voluntarily end attunement by spending another {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest} with the item, unless the item is cursed.

entries.name: Variant: Simpler Attunement
entries: If you prefer a simpler method, you can instead allow your characters to have a total of three attunement slots. If you do so, enhanced items should only take one attunement slot, regardless of rarity.

entries.name: Cursed Items
entries: Some enhanced items bear curses that bedevil their users, sometimes long after a user has stopped using an item. An enhanced item's description specifies whether the item is cursed. Most methods of identifying items, such as the {@i analyze} {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}, fail to reveal such a curse, although lore might hint at it. A curse should be a surprise to the item's user when the curse's effects are revealed.
Attunement to a cursed item can't be ended voluntarily unless the curse is broken first.

entries.name: Enhanced Item Categories
entries: Enhanced items fall into different categories depending on the type of enhanced item. Some categories, such as weapons and armor, are obvious. Others are less so.

entries.name: Adventuring Gear
entries: Items that don't fall in one of the other categories are considered adventuring gear. They might be worn items, such as boots or a {@item Jetpack|sw5e-phb|jetpack}, or hand-held item like a {@item Holocron|sw5e-phb|holocron}. This category is a catch-all for for items that don't fit in other categories.

entries.name: Armor
entries: Unless an armor's description says otherwise, armor must be worn for its enhanced properties to function.

Some suits of enhanced armor specify the type of armor they are, such as durasteel armor or {@item Combat suit|sw5e-phb|combat suit}, or the category in which they fall, such as light or {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}. If an enhanced armor doesn't specify its armor type, you may choose the type or determine it randomly.

entries.name: Consumables
entries: Typically, consumables are single use (unless the description says otherwise). Once a consumable is used, it takes effect immediately and is rendered useless.

The value of consumables, due to their impermanent nature, is typically half that of permanent enhanced items. Consumables are sub-categorized by their type: {@b {@i Adrenals.}} Adrenals are designed to give a short term boost to a creature, like increased {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. Adrenal effects rarely last longer than a minute.
{@b {@i Ammunition.}} Ammunition is unique sources of power or temporary enhancements for weapons.
{@b {@i Barriers.}} Barriers offer temporary protection, usually to a single damage type, and rarely last longer than a minute.
{@b {@i Explosives.}} Explosives, such as cryo grenades or thermal detonators, are designed to cause an effect in a radius that varies depending on their nature.
{@b {@i Medpacs.}} Medpacs are used to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to creatures other than droids and constructs.
{@b {@i Poisons.}} Poisons are used to incapacitate or harm beasts and humanoids.
{@b {@i Stimpacs.}} Stimpacs offer boosts to creatures, like increasing an ability score, that typically last for an hour or more.

{@b {@i Substances.}} Substances are often illicit, such as spice or death sticks, or legal and common, like beer or wine. Substances confer a benefit at risk of addiction. Substances are discussed further later in this chapter.
{@b {@i Technology.}} {@skill Technology|sw5e-phb} consumables are used to enhance interactions with technology and other uses, including repairing droids and constructs.

entries.name: Cybernetic Augmentations
entries: Cybernetic augmentations are enhancements built in to biological creatures, such as beasts or humanoids. They come in the form of replacements, which replace a physical body part, or enhancements, which simply augment a creature. Cybernetic augmentations are discussed further later in this chapter.

entries.name: Droid Customizations
entries: Droid customizations are items that can enhance a droid in some way. They come in the form of parts, which replace a physical droid part, or protocols, which enhance the droid's functions in some way. Droid customizations are discussed later in this chapter.

entries.name: Focuses
entries: Focuses are sub-categorized depending on what type of casting they augment: force or tech.

{@b {@i Force.}} Force focuses are used to augment the casting of {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. The most common type of force focuses are focus generators, which are held in the hand of the forcecaster. Force focuses are not required to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

{@b {@i Tech.}} Tech focuses are used to augment the casting of {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. The most common type of tech focuses are wristpads, which are worn on the forearm of the techcaster. Unlike force focuses, tech focuses are required to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.
A character can only benefit from one focus at a time. Once per round you can switch which focus you are benefiting from (no action required).

entries.name: Modifiable Items
entries: Some enhanced items come with vacant slots for item modifications, which improve the enhanced item in some way. Typically, though not always, enhanced items have either built in properties or vacant modification slots, but not both. Modifiable items—and their modifications—are discussed further later in this chapter.

entries.name: Shields
entries: Like armor, unless the description says otherwise, the {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} must be actively wielded for its enhanced properties to function.

Some {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shields} specify the category in which they fall, such as light {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} generator or any heavy {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}. If an enhanced {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} doesn't specify its category, you may choose the category or determine it randomly.

entries.name: Weapons
entries: Whether crafted for a nefarious or benevolent purpose, weapons are among the most coveted of enhanced items.

Some enhanced items specify the type of weapon they are in their descriptions, such as a lightsaber or {@item Assault cannon|sw5e-phb|assault cannon}, or the category in which they fall, such as {@filter vibroweapon|items|type=martial weapon} or {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true}.  If an enhanced weapon doesn't specific its weapon type, you may choose the type or determine it randomly.

entries.name: Awarding Enhanced Items
entries: Enhanced items are prized by adventurers are all sorts, often serving as the main reward for an adventurer. This section helps determine which enhanced items end up in the characters' possession.

entries.name: Distribution
entries: The Minor and Major Enhanced Items by Rarity tables below show the number of enhanced items a party of four should encounter during a campaign, culminating in 100 enhanced items accumulated by 20th level. The tables show much many of those items are meant to be handed out during the five tiers of play. The second and third tiers (levels 5-8 and 9-12, respectively) are intended to be when characters receive the majority of enhanced items, since these are the tiers where the majority of campaigns occur.

entries.name: Minor and Major Items
entries: The most common distinction between minor and major enhanced items is attunement. All items that require attunement should be treated as major enhanced items. On the other hand, all consumables and item modifications should be treated as minor enhanced items. Many items, however, do not easily fall into those two categories. Generally, if the item has a significant impact on one of the three pillars of adventure—exploration, social interaction, or combat—but does not require attunement, it should nonetheless be treated as a major item.

For instance, armor +1 does not require attunement, but it has a significant impact in combat, so it should be treated as major. Mag-lock boots, however, don't significantly impact any aspect of gameplay, and thus should be treated as minor.

You decide when to place an item in an adventure that you're creating or modifying usually because you think the story calls for an enhanced item, the characters need one, or the players would be especially pleased to get one.
When you want to select an item as treasure for an encounter, the Minor and Major Enhanced Items by Rarity tables serve as your item budget, as follows:

items: {@b 1.} Jot down a copy of the table in your notes, so that you can make adjustments to the numbers as you select items to be placed in an adventure.

{@b 2.} Refer to the line in the Character Level column that corresponds to the level of the player characters in your game. The entries in that row of the table indicate the total number of items that would be appropriate for the characters to receive by the end of the tier represented by that row.
{@b 3.} Choose an enhanced item of any rarity for which the entry in this row is not 0.
{@b 4.} When the characters obtain an item, modify your notes to indicate which part of your budget this expenditure came from by subtracting 1 from the appropriate entry in the table.

entries: In the future, if you choose an item of a rarity that's not available in the current tier but is still available in a lower tier, deduct the item from the lower tier. If all lower tiers also have no items available of a given rarity, deduct the item from a higher tier.

entries.name: Choosing Items Piecemeal
entries: If you prefer a more free-form method of choosing enhanced items, simply select each enhanced item you want to give out; then, when th e characters acquire one, deduct it from the Enhanced Items by Rarity tables in your notes. Whenever you do so, start with the lowest level tier, and deduct the item from the first number you come across in the appropriate rarity column for the item, whether it's minor or major. If that tier doesn't have a number greater than 0 for that rarity, go up a tier until you find one that does, and deduct the enhanced item from that number. Following this process, you will zero out each row of the table in order, going from the lowest levels to the highest.

entries.name: Generating New Enhanced Items
entries: As a GM, you can easily generate new enhanced items by combining the effects of two like items, provided those items have the same type and subtype (if present). For instance, you could combine the effects of two item modification (augments) to create a new, higher rarity augment, but you couldn't combine the effects of a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} and a suit of armor to create a new item in this way. When you do so, you want to combine the rarities of the items whose effects you are combining by assigning a point value to each item. A standard item has a value of 1, premium has a value of 2, and so on up to an artifact's value of 6. Add the points for the items you are combining to determine the new item's rarity. For instance, if you combine the effects a premium (2 points) augment with a prototype (3 points) augment, you end up with a new legendary augment due to the combined total of 5 points. You can't exceed 6 points when combining objects in this way. If the two items you are combining confer a like bonus, such as a bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} or the save DC of {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, that bonus should not exceed +3. If the items already include rules governing the maximum value that item could provide, such as a keen weapon modification, you would instead follow the guidelines provided by that item.

entries.name: Overstocking an Adventure
entries: The enhanced item tables in this chapter are based on the number of items the characters are expected to receive, not the number of items that are available in an adventure. When creating or modifying an adventure, assume that the characters won't find all of the items you place in it, unless most of the loot is in easy-to-find locations.

entries.name: Are Enhanced Items Necessary?
entries: Ultimately, this is a question that can only be answered at your table. Some players are more loot driven, while others prefer to focus on story. Generally, a normal campaign assumes that enhanced items appear sporadically and are a boon. Consequently, if your player characters obtain an inordinate amount of enhanced items, encounters might become progressively trivial. As a GM, you have to worry about maintaining that balance.
The value of an enhanced item varies depending on the rarity of the item, as shown below in the Enhanced Item Value by Rarity table.

Using the Enhanced Item Value by Rarity table, you then assign prices to the available items, based on their rarity. Halve the price of any consumable item, such as a {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac} or explosive, or item modification when using the table to determine an item's value.

entries.name: Determine Values Randomly
entries: Alternatively, you can determine the value of enhanced items randomly. To do so, you should first roll percentile dice twice, keeping the higher total. Then, you should multiply the result by the modifier, depending on the item's rarity, as shown below in the Value Modifier by Rarity table.

If item value falls below the base threshold for that rarity, you might instead use the base for that rarity. For instance, if I want to determine the value of a prototype item, I first roll percentile dice twice. I get the results of 63 and 22, so I keep the 63 since it's the higher number. I then multiply that number by the value modifier for prototype (250 cr), ending up with an item value of 15,750 cr (63 x 250 cr). If I instead had rolled 11 and 16 on the percentile dice rolls, however, I would have ended up with an item value of 4,000 cr (16 x 250 cr). Since this falls below the minimum value threshold for prototype items (5,000 cr), you could instead use the minimum.
To reflect the availability of enhanced items in your campaign, you can apply a penalty or bonus, as appropriate to your setting, when resolving the d100 roll determining enhanced item values.

When determining the value for an enhanced item that has an unenhanced version, such as a {@item Medpac|sw5e-phb|medpac} or a {@item Blaster rifle|sw5e-phb}, instead of replacing with the value determined by the rolls above, add the result to the unenhanced item's value.

entries.name: Modifiable Items
entries: Some enhanced items come with fixed properties. Other enhanced items, called chassis, are more customizable.

entries.name: Modifying Equipment
entries: Modifying an item requires three key components: a modifiable item chassis, a modification to install, and the appropriate tools. An item can only be modified by someone proficient with appropriate tools, as shown in the Item Specific Tools Tools by Item table in this chapter.

entries.name: Modifiable Item Chassis
entries: Every item chassis comes with at least four modification slots, increasing to six at higher rarities, as determined by the chassis's rarity, as shown below in the Modification Slots by Rarity table.

Every modifiable item chassis has four base slots, determined by its type. Prototype and advanced modifiable item chassis also have one augment slot in addition to the four base slots for their type, while legendary and artifact have two. A modifiable item chassis only requires attunement and is considered enhanced if it has at least one modification installed.

A modifiable item chassis can only include modifications of the same rarity or a lesser rarity. For instance, if you have a prototype modifiable item chassis, you can modify it with standard, premium, and prototype modifications. However, the item's nature does not allow it to support higher rarity modifications.

entries.name: Installing Modifications
entries: Installing a modification takes one hour and requires an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with the appropriate tool, as shown in the Item Specific Tools Tools by Item table in this chapter. The DC for the check is determined by the rarity of the modification being installed, as shown below in the Installation/Removal DC by Rarity table.
On a success, the modification is correctly installed. On a failure, the modification is not installed, and you must wait 24 hours before you can try again.

entries.name: Removing Modifications
entries: Removing a modification requires an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with the appropriate tool, as shown in the Item Specific Tools table. The DC for the check is determined by the rarity of the modification being removed, as shown above in the Installation/Removal DC by Rarity table.
On a success, the modification is removed and salvaged. On a failure, the modification is removed but destroyed.

entries.name: Upgrading Modifiable Item Chassis
entries: Modifiable item chassis can have their rarity upgraded over time. An item can only be upgraded by someone proficient with the appropriate tools, and it can only be upgraded one rarity step at a time. Modifying a chassis takes eight hours and requires an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with the appropriate tool. The DC for the check is determined by the rarity to which the chassis is being upgraded, as shown in the Installation/Removal DC by Rarity table above. Additionally, upgrading the rarity of a chassis requires an appropriate rare material, as discussed in the Crafting downtime activity. Upgrading a modifiable item chassis has no effect on any modifications currently installed in the chassis.

On a success, the modifiable item chassis is upgraded to the new rarity. On a failure, the modifiable item chassis is not upgraded, you must wait 24 hours before you can try again, and you must roll a {@dice d20}. If you roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, one currently installed modification is destroyed. If the chassis has more than one modification installed, the GM should determine which modification is destroyed randomly.

entries.name: Color Crystals
entries: In addition to the modifications unique to themselves, {@filter all lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} come with a slot for a color crystal. Typically, newly created {@filter lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} come with one of the more common color variants, such as green, blue, or red. Occasionally, a character might come across a more scarce color crystal. When determining what color crystal a {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} comes with, the GM can choose for the player, or have the player make a universal {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} check with proficiency. The result of the check affects the color of the crystal, as shown below in the {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} Color Crystal Modifier table.

entries.caption: Forcecasting Color Crystal Modifier

entries: The {@b d100 Roll Modifier} is added to the percentile dice rolled for the Color Crystal table, which is discussed below.

Once a player has made their {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} check to discover a {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} color crystal, the player rolls percentile dice and consults the Color Crystal table below, applying a modifier based on the result of their {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} check.
This table includes the most common and desirable color crystals. More extensive options can be awarded at the discretion of the GM.

A player can choose the color crystal that is the result of their percentile dice rolled, or they can choose one that falls below it. For instance, if the player rolls a 91 and finds a viridian color crystal, they could instead choose a yellow color crystal, as if they had rolled a 63.

entries.name: Augments
entries: Augments are intended to offer features universal across items, such as an increase to an ability score or augmenting a class feature.
You can't have two of the same augment in a single chassis, but you can have multiples of an augment, each in its own chassis.

{@b {@i Installing Augments in Other Items.}} Additionally, a character proficient in {@item Tinker's implements|sw5e-phb|tinker's implements} can add modification slots for augments to items that lack them. First, the character must spend one uninterrupted hour tinkering with the item, which can be done over a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, with their {@item Tinker's implements|sw5e-phb|tinker's implements}. The character must then make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with {@item Tinker's implements|sw5e-phb|tinker's implements}. On a result of less than 20, the item gains no augment slots, and you must wait 24 hours before you can try again. On a result of 20 or higher, the item gains one augment slot, to a maximum of one augment slot. On a result of 30 or higher, the item gains a two augment slots, to a maximum of two augment slots. Adding augment slots to an item causes that item to require attunement, if it didn't already. An item can't support augments of higher rarity than the item's rarity.

entries.name: Variant: Common Modifications
entries: Modifying equipment is a common expectation of adventurers foraying through the worlds of {@i Star Wars}. This rule treats all potential modifiable items—that is, the eight categories listed in this chapter—as unmodified standard rarity chassis. For example, every unenhanced {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} you find while adventuring, or for sale in a market, comes with vacant modification slots for {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} modifications.
Additionally, all modifications of standard rarity should be available for purchase from appropriate vendors without using the Buying Enhanced Items downtime activity.
Note that all chassis of premium or higher rarity should still be treated as enhanced items for the purposes of distribution.

entries.name: Cybernetic Augmentations
entries: Some characters are dissatisfied with their inborn gifts, while some are simply looking to augment their natural prowess. The less fortunate, however, might find themselves missing a limb. For all of these characters, cybernetic augmentations suit a purpose.

entries.name: Augmenting Creatures
entries: Augmenting a creature with cybernetic enhancements requires three key components: a valid target for the augmentation, an augmentation to install, and {@item Biotech's implements|sw5e-phb|biotech's implements}. A creature can only be modified by someone with proficiency in {@item Biotech's implements|sw5e-phb|biotech's implements}.

entries.name: Valid Targets
entries: Typically, only beasts and humanoids are valid targets for augmentations. A creature can support a number of cybernetic augmentations equal to their {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Augmentation Time
entries: It takes 8 hours to install an augmentation in a Medium creature. The time it takes to install an augmentation in a creature of another size varies based on the size of the target, as shown below in the Creature Size Time Modifier table below.
For instance, to install an augmentation in a Medium creature takes 8 hours. To install an augmentation in a Huge creature, however, it takes 40 hours (5 x 8).
The installer works 8 hours per day. It costs 100 credits per hour if the operation is performed by an NPC.

In addition to the side effects associated with each augmentation, your body undergoes changes, depending on how many augmentations you adopt, as shown below in the Cybernetic Augmentation Side Effects table.

rows: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that deal ion damage.
You have vulnerability to ion damage.
You count as a droid for powers that affect only droids or constructs.

entries.name: Installing Augmentations
entries: In addition to the time and cost requirement, installing an augmentation requires an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with {@item Biotech's implements|sw5e-phb|biotech's implements}. The DC for the check is determined by the rarity of the augmentation being installed, as shown in the Installation/Removal DC by Rarity table in this chapter

On a success, the augmentation is correctly installed. On a failure, the augmentation is not installed, the time and credits are spent, and you must wait 24 hours before you can try again. Additionally, on a failure, the recipient suffers another effect, depending on the type of augmentation installed:

items: {@b Enhancement:} On a failure, the recipient suffers one level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}.

{@b Replacement:} On a failure, the recipient loses the ability to use the part being replaced for a period of time equal to the time it would take to install the replacement. For instance, to install an arm replacement in a Huge creature it takes 40 hours, performed over five days. If, at the end of the five day period, the installer fails the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with {@item Biotech's implements|sw5e-phb|biotech's implements}, the Huge creature loses the ability to use that arm for five days.

entries.name: Removing Augmentations
entries: Removing an augmentation takes half the time and credits it would to install, and requires an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with {@item Biotech's implements|sw5e-phb|biotech's implements}. The DC for the check is determined by the rarity of the augmentation being removed, as shown in the Installation/Removal DC by Rarity table in this chapter
On a success, the augmentation is removed and salvaged. On a failure, the augmentation is removed but destroyed.
Additionally, if removing a replacement augmentation, the recipient loses the ability to use the missing part until it receives another suitable replacement.

entries.name: Augmentation Categories
entries: Two major categories of cybernetic augmentations exist in the galaxy: enhancements and replacements.

entries.name: Enhancements
entries: Enhancements bestowed new abilities or improved the recipient in some fashion. Enhancements included skeletal reinforcement, subcutaneous communications hardware, and weapon mounts. Some enhancements have visible external components, while others were hidden beneath the skin.

entries.name: Replacements
entries: Replacements are prosthetic or artificial units intended to replace limbs and damaged organs. Common replacements provided no benefits other than duplicating the essential functions of their biological counterparts. In appearance, a cybernetic replacement could be recognizably artificial or virtually indistinguishable from the real thing.

entries.name: Droid Customizations
entries: Droids vary in form and function. Beyond simply their droid classification and subtype, many droids—or their owners—crave further customizability. Droid customizations are designed for this purpose.

entries.name: Customizing Droids
entries: Customizing a droid with droid-specific equipment requires three key components: a droid with a valid slot for the equipment, a piece of equipment to install, and {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements}. A droid can only be customized by someone with proficiency in {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements}.

entries.name: Valid Targets
entries: Only droids are valid targets for droid customizations. A droid's motor can support two droid customizations, and can be upgraded to support up to six customizations.

entries.name: Customization Time
entries: It takes 8 hours to install a customization in a Medium droid. The time it takes to install a customization in a droid of another size varies based on the size of the target, as shown in the Droid Size Time Modifier table below.
For instance, to install a customization in a Medium droid takes 8 hours. To install an augmentation in a Huge droid, however, it takes 40 hours (5 x 8).
The installer works 8 hours per day. It costs 100 credits per hour if the operation is performed by an NPC.

entries.name: Motor Upgrading
entries: A droid's motor can be upgraded to support more customizations, up to a maximum of six customizations. To upgrade the motor in a Medium droid, it takes 8 hours and a number of credits depending on the total number of slots the upgraded motor grants, as shown below  in the Total Slots Upgrade Cost table.
The time and cost it takes to upgrade a motor in a droid of another size varies based on the size of the target, as shown in the Droid Size Time Modifier table.

For instance, to upgrade a Medium droid's motor from 2 slots to 3 slots, it takes 8 hours and 2,000 cr. To upgrade a Huge droid's motor from 3 slots to 4 slots, however, it takes 40 hours (5 x 8) and 50,000 cr (5 x 10,000).
The installer works 8 hours a day. It costs 100 credits per hour if the operation is performed by an NPC.

entries.name: Installing Customizations
entries: In addition to the time and cost requirement, installing a customization requires an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements}. The DC for the check is determined by the rarity of the customization being installed, as shown in the Installation/Removal DC by Rarity table in this chapter
On a success, the customization is correctly installed. On a failure, the customization is not installed, the time and credits are spent, and you must wait 24 hours before you can try again.

entries.name: Removing Customizations
entries: Removing a customization takes half the time and credits it would to install, and requires an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with {@item Astrotech's implements|sw5e-phb|astrotech's implements}. The DC for the check is determined by the rarity of the customization being removed, as shown in the Installation/Removal DC by Rarity table in this chapter
On a success, the customization is removed and salvaged. On a failure, the customization is removed but destroyed.

entries.name: Customization Categories
entries: Two major categories of droid customizations exist in the galaxy: parts and protocols.

entries.name: Parts
entries: Parts typically enhance or replace the features of a droid. Additional arms, integrated {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} generators or weapons, or built-in repulsor lifts. You can't have more parts than your Strength, Dexterity or Constitution modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

entries.name: Protocols
entries: Protocols bestow new abilities or improvements on the target droid. Typically, they take the shape of systems improvements and offer no visible indication that they exist. You can't have more protocols than your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

data.name: Chapter 8: Tool Proficiencies
entries: Tool proficiencies are a useful way to highlight a character's background and talents. At the game table, though, the use of tools sometimes overlaps with the use of skills, and it can be unclear how to use them together in certain situations. This section offers various ways that tools can be used in the game.
To make tool proficiencies more attractive choices for the characters, you can use the methods outlined below.

entries.name: Tool Descriptions
entries: The following sections go into detail about the tools presented in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5}, as well as those present in the {@i Player's Handbook}, offering advice on how to use them in a campaign.
The first paragraph in each description gives details on what a set of tools is made up of. A character who is proficient with a tool knows how to use all of its component parts.

entries.name: Skills
entries: Every tool potentially provides bonuses on a check when used in conjunction with certain skills, provided a character is proficient with both the tool and the skill. Each tool grants bonuses to three skills.

With respect to skills, the system is mildly abstract in terms of what a tool proficiency represents; essentially, it assumes that a character who has proficiency with a tool also has learned about facets of the trade or profession that are not necessarily associated with the use of the tool.

{@b {@i Advantage.}} If the use of a tool and the use of a skill both apply to a check, and a character is proficient with the tool and the skill, consider allowing the character to make the check with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. This simple benefit can go a long way toward encouraging players to pick up tool proficiencies. In the tool descriptions that follow, this benefit is often expressed as additional insight (or something similar), which translates into an increased chance that the check will be a success.

{@b {@i Added Benefit.}} Additionally, consider giving characters who have both a relevant skill and a relevant tool proficiency an added benefit on a successful check. This benefit might be in the form of more detailed information or could simulate the effect of a different sort of successful check. For instance, a character proficient with constructor's implements makes a successful Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) check to find a secret door in a wall. Not only does the character notice the door's presence, but you decide that the tool proficiency entitles the character to an automatic success on an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|sw5e-phb}) check to determine how to open the door.

entries.name: Other Tools
entries: Additionally, at the GM's discretion, certain tools might grant bonuses when used in conjunction with another tool, provided a character is proficient with both. For instance, if a character is proficient with both munitions kits and {@item Armstech's implements|sw5e-phb|armstech's implements}, you might grant them {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on checks they make with either tool.

entries.name: Special Use
entries: Proficiency with a tool usually brings with it a particular benefit in the form of a special use, as described in this paragraph. During a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can only activate the special use of one of your tools.
A table at the end of each section lists activities that a tool can be used to perform, and suggested DCs for the necessary {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks}.

entries.name: Archaeologist Kit
entries: This kit contains instruments used to carefully collect crystals, gems, relics, and other heirlooms. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to any {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} you make to classify, collect, and polish gems and relics.

entries.name: Survival
entries: When searching in the wild, you can more easily search for places that might house relics.

entries.name: Investigation
entries: You can easily spot the location of potential gemstones or other precious relics.

entries.name: Persuasion
entries: When bartering while precious stones or relics are involved, you can more easily negotiate a fair price.

Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can make a DC 15 archaelogist kit check to temporarily improve a {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} or focus generator. To use this benefit, you must have archaelogist kit with you, and the object must be within reach. On a success, once before your next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, a character wielding this {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} can gain a bonus to one weapon damage roll, or focus generator can gain a bonus to one force damage or healing roll. This bonus is a die, with a maximum value equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. If you have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the tool, this die's maximum is instead equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Armormech's Implements
entries: {@item Armormech's implements|sw5e-phb} include all of the necessary components to allow you to work raw materials to craft or repair damage to armor and shields.

entries.name: Lore
entries: Your {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} lends you additional insight when examining armor and shields.

entries.name: Investigation
entries: You can spot clues and make deductions that others might overlook when an investigation involves armor and shields.

entries.name: Stealth
entries: Your greater understanding of armor you—or your allies—wear allows for more cautious movement.

Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can make a DC 15 {@item Armormech's implements|sw5e-phb|armormech's implements} check to temporarily improve a suit of armor or a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}. To use this benefit, you must have {@item Armormech's implements|sw5e-phb|armormech's implements} with you, and the object must be within reach. On a success, once before your next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, a character wearing this armor or wielding this {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} can gain a bonus to AC against one attack. This bonus is a die, with a maximum value equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. If you have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the tool, this die's maximum is instead equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Artillerist's Kit
entries: Artillerist's kits contains all the necessary equipment to create, repair, and modify turrets.

entries.name: Lore
entries: Your proficiency allows you to more readily discern the history of any turrets you encounter.

entries.name: Investigation and Perception
entries: Your experience lets you more readily identify aftermarket modifications in turrets.

Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can make a DC 15 artillerist's kit check to temporarily improve a turret. To use this benefit, you must have an artillerist's kit with you, and the object must be within reach. On a success, once before your next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, this turret can gain a bonus to one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} or a bonus to one save DC. This bonus is a die, with a maximum value equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}. If you have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the tool, this die's maximum is instead equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Artist's Implements
entries: Artist's implements include all of the necessary components to create and store art.

entries.name: Lore
entries: Your {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} aids you in uncovering lore of any sort that is attached to a work of art, such as the mystical properties of a painting or the origins of a strange mural found in a dungeon.

entries.name: Investigation and Perception
entries: When you inspect a painting or a similar work of visual art, your knowledge of the practices behind creating it can grant you additional insight.

Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can make a DC 15 artist's implements check to create a depiction of an event, person, or other noteworthy object. To use this benefit, you must have artist's implements with you. On a success, you create a rendition that perfectly captures the event in question, provided the event happened no more than one day ago. If you have {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in the tool, you can instead capture an event that happened no more than one week ago.

entries: Proficiency with brewer's kit gives you additional insight on Intelligence ({@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}) checks concerning events that involve alcohol as a significant element.

entries.name: Medicine
entries: This tool proficiency grants additional insight when you treat anyone suffering from alcohol poisoning or when you can use alcohol to dull pain.

entries.name: Persuasion
entries: A stiff drink can help soften the hardest heart. Your proficiency with brewer's kit can help you ply someone with drink, giving them just enough alcohol to mellow their mood .

Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can make a DC 15 brewer's kit check to hone or reduce the addictive properties of an alcoholic beverage within reach. To use this benefit, you must have a brewer's kit, and the alcoholic beverage must be within reach. If a creature consumes the alcoholic beverage before the end of your next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, they have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} (your choice) on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} made to avoid the low and addiction.

rows: Detect poison or impurities in a drink

entries.name: Chef's Kit
entries: This kit includes all of the necessary implements to prepare and serve food to up to six people. Proficiency with this kit lets you add your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to any {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability checks} you make to identify food. Also, proficiency with this kit is required to create field rations.

entries.name: Lore
entries: Your knowledge of cooking techniques allow you to assess the social patterns involved in a culture's eating habits.

entries.name: Medicine
entries: When administering treatment, you can transform medicine that is bitter or sour into a pleasing concoction.

entries.name: Survival
entries: When foraging for food, you can make do with ingredients you scavenge that others would be unable to transform into nourishing meals.
{@i Feature that utilizes the tool in some capacity.}

entries.name: Prepare Meals
entries: Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can make a DC 15 chef's

As part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, you can prepare a tasty meal that helps your companions regain their strength. You and up to five creatures of your choice regain 1 extra hit point per Hit Die spent during a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, provided you have access to your {@item Chef's kit|sw5e-phb|chef's kit} and sufficient food. During a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can prepare and serve a meal that helps you and your allies recover from the rigors of adventuring, provided you have suitable food, {@item Chef's kit|sw5e-phb|chef's kit}, and other supplies on hand. The meal serves up to six people, and each person who eats it regains two additional Hit Dice at the end of the {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. In addition, those who partake of the meal have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against disease for the next 24 hours.

rows: Spot poison or impurities in food
